nodes.name: Tavily: Web Search
nodes.notes: Grounds the LLM in real search results instead of asking it to answer from training data. Requires the TAVILY_API_KEY n8n Variable (free tier: 1,000 searches/month, no card - https://tavily.com). Unlike Serper (Google's raw operator syntax), Tavily accepts plain natural-language queries with no site:/OR/parentheses restrictions.

nodes.name: Aggregate Search Results
nodes.notes: Build Search Query fans out into one item per job title, so Tavily: Web Search runs once per title (n8n's default per-item execution). This node collects all of those responses back into a single deduped result set (by URL) before the LLM ever sees them, so Call LLM (Web Search) still runs exactly once per ICP run against the combined pool.

nodes.name: Call LLM (Web Search)
nodes.notes: Search results are enriched before reaching the LLM with an extractedCompany field: for LinkedIn profile URLs it's parsed deterministically from the page header (name/company/location lines); for any other result (company team/leadership/about pages, press releases) it's guessed from the page title via a few common patterns ("X - Leadership", "Leadership - X", "Name - Title | X", "X - Team"). LinkedIn is never required to extract a candidate - it's one recognized source among several (see the OR wording in Build Search Query's tail string), and this same extraction runs for every result type. Reads from Aggregate Search Results (the combined pool across every job-title query - up to 10 titles x 20 results each as of the latest volume bump, deduped by URL - not a single Tavily call) and uses an 8192 output-token budget so a larger pool doesn't get truncated into fewer candidates than it should find.

nodes.name: Parse Candidates JSON
nodes.notes: OpenRouter/OpenAI-style response: the model's answer is a plain string at choices[0].message.content (no block array like Anthropic's format). OpenRouter sometimes proxies an upstream provider error (e.g. Nvidia overloaded) back as a 200 response body with an `error` field instead of `choices` — handled below so that shows up as a real message, not a JSON.parse crash.

nodes.name: Normalize Split Candidate
nodes.notes: Split Out (previous node) nests each split element under its original field name (candidates) instead of flattening it, so { firstName, company, ... } arrives here as { candidates: { firstName, company, ... } }. That silently broke IF: Has Company (checking a field that no longer existed at top level) and corrupted the final payload sent to the app (422 Required). This unwraps it back to a flat candidate object.

nodes.name: Hunter: Email Finder
nodes.notes: Finds a real, verified email for a candidate by company + name. Requires the HUNTER_API_KEY n8n Variable (https://hunter.io) — free tier gives 25 searches/month. Only called when the candidate has a company name, since Hunter requires company or domain to search against.

nodes.name: Apply Hunter Result
nodes.notes: Only accepts Hunter's email if its own confidence score is >=50 - never fabricates or lowers the bar below what Hunter itself considers reliable.
